thread:
jamie (oncall): paging: sudden GPU memory collapse on streaming decode pool, we're seeing request drops and partial responses. paging @rita @ryan :rotating_light:
incident-bot: ALERT: decode-pool-4 memory spike -> OOM kills x3 in 3m, auto-throttle engaged. Incident ID: INC-179555
rita (ops): on it. checking pods and node metrics now. any known customers impacted?
maya (cs): CS: Ticket #C-8921 opened — customer reports repeated disconnects and truncated responses. they provided a sample request id. can we confirm cause before I update?
ryan (runtime): looking at container logs: repeated CUDA exceptions then SIGKILL. suspect runaway generation from a client sending huge max_output header. quick dump of recent requests shows several with header `x-max-output: 10000`.
jamie (oncall): ok. mitigation plan: 1) apply a temporary per-route max_tokens cap at 256 2) enable cpu-fallback for this route 3) quarantine offending API key. rita can you push the route override?
rita (ops): I can. applying route override now — will patch control plane and bubble to edge.
rita (ops): ```bash
# quick rollback-friendly override
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/routes/abc123/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"max_tokens":256, "fallback":"cpu"}'
# response: 200 OK
```
incident-bot: Change applied: route override for route abc123 (max_tokens=256, fallback=cpu). Telemetry: tail memory usage down ~70% within 30s.
ryan (runtime): confirmed — pool memory trending down, no new OOMs on decode-pool-4. found offending API key: xyz-334 associated with client-id stream-bot-334; requests show header `x-max-output: 10000` and persistent streaming sessions that grew kv-cache.
jamie (oncall): quarantine the API key and notify CS. also leave override for 15m while we monitor.
maya (cs): quarantined api key xyz-334 and notified the customer contact. CS asked for request ids and gave an interim explanation. updating ticket now (C-8921).
rita (ops): nodes stable, a couple container restarts but no additional OOMs. keeping throttle for 15m, then will try increasing to 512 in a controlled manner if stable.
ryan (runtime): filing followup: create RFC to add server-side validation for `x-max-output` and a hard cap at the router; also add an alert rule for header values >2000. tagging eng-runtime, sdk, and security.
jamie (oncall): short customer-facing note draft: "We mitigated a memory runaway caused by an oversized max_tokens header; temporary limits were applied to prevent further request drops; no data was lost. We'll follow up with a permanent validation and SDK patch." Maya can you send?
maya (cs): sending now. customer responded appreciative of quick mitigation. CS will keep the ticket open for one follow-up.
incident-bot: INC-179555 status: mitigated -> monitoring. no new OOM events in the last 10m. closing pager.
jamie (oncall): thanks everyone. post-incident: add runbook step to quarantine keys quickly and to auto-apply short token caps on sudden memory surges. ryan — prioritise SDK header validation next sprint.
ryan (runtime): will do. creating work item now.
maya (cs): I'll add the customer update to the incident notes and mark CS check-ins for next 24h.
rita (ops): keeping an eye on telemetry for 1h, will escalate if any recurrence.
